### Settling Disputes Among Believers
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/settling-disputes-among-believers
Passage: 1 Corinthians 6:4-6
Points:
- Paul rebukes believers for dragging petty interpersonal disputes before secular judges rather than resolving them within the church.
- The apostle's prohibition targets trivial, everyday grievances between Christians, not criminal acts or severe legal violations.
- Resorting to pagan courts exposed the Corinthians' spiritual pride and demonstrated a lack of true Christian wisdom.
- Airing internal conflicts before unbelievers compromises the church's public witness and dishonors the gospel of reconciliation.
- Christians ought to exhaust all avenues of private arbitration, relying on civil courts only when unavoidable.

### The Legal Swamp, Part One
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-june-6-7-2009-11604437.html
Passage: 1 Corinthians 6:1-8
Points:
- Society promotes a self-centered, litigious mindset focused strictly on demanding individual rights.
- Christians fall into this same trap by suing fellow believers instead of pursuing direct reconciliation.
- Believers often live as though the clear instructions of 1 Corinthians 6:1-8 do not apply to them.
- While civil law serves a necessary purpose against evil, believers must handle conflicts with grace.
- Securing a courtroom victory is never worth compromising Christian love and damaging one's soul.
